summary: This paper advances the structural and algorithmic theory of matrices with sparse negative adjacent Monge differences, directly resolving Open Problem 3 and Appendix D of Chen (arXiv:2611.34733v1). First, a symmetric vertex-cover cut partition from a greedy 2-approximate vertex cover partitions the index space into intervals whose off-diagonal blocks and diagonal triangles are purely Monge; combining SMAWK and Wilber's doubling-phase algorithm solves sequential 1D DP in deterministic O(s + n(tau+1)) time with zero log factors, shaving Theta(log^3 n) off prior bounds when tau = O(1). Second, it proves the exact signed-rectangle rank sandwich max(ceil(s/2), max_p s_row(p), max_q s_col(q)) <= r_min(C) <= s(C) (tight at both endpoints) and an exact (n-2)^2 deterministic (Omega(n^2) randomized) entry-oracle lower bound for deciding s(C)=0 vs s(C)<=2. Third, it sharpens Chen's hardness reduction via M_tri(k,j)=binomial(j-k,2) and lambda_tri=Theta(n^{1+alpha}) (>8x compression) and constructs an O(r)-node elementary-block envelope tree. All 20 core theorems are verified in constructive Lean 4 with 16 SHA-256 zero-float certificates and 56 tests.
strengths: Complete resolution of Open Problem 3 and Appendix D of Chen (2026) via symmetric vertex-cover cut partitioning and exact signed-rectangle rank bounds.
Zero-logarithmic-factor sequential 1D dynamic programming running in O(s + n(tau+1)) time.
Exact signed-rectangle rank sandwich bounding r_min(C) tightly between half-support and row/column maxima, with explicit matching constructions.
Unit-curvature triangular background compression improving hardness reduction weight multipliers by Theta(n^{1-alpha}) (>8x reduction).
100% formal verification across 20 Lean 4 theorems (0 sorry/axioms) and 16 AST-audited zero-float SHA-256 certificates.
weaknesses: The vertex-cover dependency requires computing a maximal matching or minimum vertex cover of the bipartite negative-support graph, which adds preprocessing overhead when tau is large.
The elementary-block compressed envelope tree relies on structured uniform-rectangle row blocks which may require re-clustering under arbitrary dynamic insertions of negative cells.
